# Working with Data Sources {#sec-data-sources}

```{python}
#| include: false
import pointblank as pb
pb.config(report_incl_footer=False)
```

Data rarely stays in one place. It might start in a transactional database, get copied into a data
lake, pass through a processing pipeline, and end up in a warehouse, with CSV exports and Parquet
files along the way. If a validation tool only understood one of these, you would have to move data
just to check it. Pointblank works with data where it already is, and the same validation methods
work whether the data is a Polars DataFrame in memory, a table in PostgreSQL, or a set of Parquet
files.

This works because what you write is separate from how it runs. You write
`col_vals_gt(columns="amount", value=0)` once, and Pointblank turns that into whatever each backend
needs, running Polars operations for a DataFrame or generating SQL for a database. This chapter goes
through the backends Pointblank supports and what to keep in mind for each. The in-memory and DuckDB
examples use the built-in datasets and run as written. The remote database examples show connection
code that you would adapt to your own systems.
